title: SC/ST apprenticeship funds diverted to general trainees in Mumbai board
dek: An audit of the Board of Apprenticeship Training in Mumbai finds that grants meant for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe apprentices were used for general category trainees, leaving the intended beneficiaries without the promised support.
theme: Misuse of reserved category funds in apprenticeship training
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Tamil Nadu was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: Apprentices from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes rely on grants-in-aid from the Board of Apprenticeship Training in Mumbai to complete their training. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India examined the board's records for the year ended March 2023 and found that Rs 17.34 crore of these reserved funds were used for apprentices belonging to the General category. The audit record states this as an irregular utilisation, but it does not name the apprentices who were affected or say how many of them there were.

The board's own account of how the funds were allocated is not included in the audit record. The audit report only provides the finding of irregular utilisation, without the board's explanation or any response from the board. This means that for the apprentices who were supposed to receive the funds, the record does not settle whether the money reached them or whether they were denied training support.

The audit record identifies the Board of Apprenticeship Training, Mumbai, as the institution responsible for the irregular utilisation. It states that the grants-in-aid meant for SC/ST apprentices were instead used for General category apprentices. The record does not provide details of the specific transactions or the period over which this occurred, beyond the year ended March 2023.

The audit's finding is based on the board's own records, which the auditors examined. The record does not include any independent verification of the apprentices' backgrounds or the actual use of the funds. Therefore, while the audit states the irregularity, it does not establish the full extent of the diversion or whether any funds were recovered.

The audit record does not say who authorised the use of SC/ST funds for General category apprentices. It also does not say whether the apprentices who were meant to benefit from the funds were aware of the diversion or whether they received any alternative support. These questions remain unanswered in the supplied evidence.

For people in India who depend on such apprenticeship programmes, the audit record confirms that a significant sum of reserved funds was not used for its intended purpose. However, it does not provide a timeline for when the irregularity occurred or the names of the officials involved. The record also does not indicate whether any corrective action has been taken since the audit.
